issue_context.title: Small overlap between buttons at the bottom of song select
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:**

There is a small (1 pixel?) overlap between the buttons at the bottom of song select.

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/27663662/64064632-7473c800-cc47-11e9-989e-70c9a1175285.png)

**osu!lazer version:** 2019.831.0
comments:
Removing from `good first issue` as there is more things concerned.

From what I think the problem is, is the `EdgeSmoothness` and the transparency the colors have when unhovered.

Discussing my findings, getting the ball rolling for alternative solutions

## Root causes

I'll try to explain in order of occurrence, as all these are connected one way or another

- ``Shearing`` causes jaggies to the ``light`` 
- ``EdgeSmoothness`` helps smooth out the artifacts caused by ``Shearing``, but
- ``EdgeSmoothness``'s ``Inflation`` causes the pixels to overflow to the neighbouring ``light``

## My Attempts
- Use ``DrawSizePreservingContainer`` is feasible for ``FooterButton`` that do not change their width, which is not applicable to ``FooterButtonsMods``. When ``ModIcons`` and ``Multiplier`` is added to the button, this attempt will scale wrongly
- Adding a spacing between the ``FooterButtons`` is not feasible either, as now the UI scaling and resolution comes into play.
- Using ``Masking = true`` can help reduce but not eliminate the number of pixels that overlap. Besides, using this will reintroduce jagged edges. 

## Potential Solutions
- Footer redesign so that the colours do not overlap
- Use skinning to overcome this issue (a la osu!stable)
- Give each ``FooterButton`` z-axis depth and do something similar to Front-to-Back pass

review_comments: this still needs proper investigation. i'd hope to avoid ui spacing specific adjustments if possible.

The UI scaling based approach was meant to counteract this remaining overlap. 

![Screenshot_20200222_214246](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43511642/75094173-cc223900-55c3-11ea-982e-6b1ab11e00a7.png)

Without the UI scaling elements, the overlap is still visible but not as obvious as before. You probably would miss it if I didn't mention that the overlap is still there. Still, it is kind of a half-hearted approach. If this is acceptable, then I would push my remaining commits and fix the conflicts. Else, I would be re-closing this PR.

Theoretically, the problems should already be solved when ``Masking=true`` is set, as it should mask the pixels outside of respective containers already. I tried investigating, but still can't determine why the pixels are "leaking out".

Does the overlap depicted above grow & shrink with size with UI scaling changes? It seems to be a pixel-ish wide in size from the attached screenshot, which makes me think it is due to blending & antialiasing at the drawable edges causing a single pixel of overlap. If it does grow then it probably is something else.

It looks like it stays at the same size, but it gets more obvious? (brighter?) when UI scale is smaller.
